chore: adaptations for nightly-2026-03-15 nightly#199

Please review this PR. At the next toolchain release this diff will land in 'master'.
Ah, I need to clean up a little here. Now that lean bundles leantar, having the fallback code for Cache to retrieve leantar itself is pointless.

@Mac Malone @Mario Carneiro we're having a problem here because leantar 0.1.18 wants to write to /tmp, but we are running it in Mathlib CI under landrun without access to /tmp.

Can you two work out a solution to this?
As this is affecting nightly-testing as well, for now I have just poked a hole in landrun for read-write access to /tmp, here and on nightly-testing.
(Feeling the pressure to keep nightly-testing green as we try to get everything sorted for v4.29.0.)

@Mac Malone, @Mario Carneiro, this PR, and nightly-testing are now failing with:

thread 'main' (123921) panicked at src/tar.rs:226:27:
called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: PersistError(Os { code: 18, kind: CrossesDevices, message: "Cross-device link" })
note: run with `RUST_BACKTRACE=1` environment variable to display a backtrace

Compressing cache
packing ./Mathlib.lean as cb567551c04acfd5.ltar

and I don't know what to do with this. My plan, unless one of you knows a better solution, is to asap revert the changes to Lean that bundled leantar, and ask that that be redone with more careful Mathlib integration testing.

There's still some other blockers for getting v4.29.0 out, but I really really need a green nightly-testing while getting that sorted.

@Mac Malone, if you have time to look at this before the next nightly release, could you ideally do the reverts yourself, or otherwise tell me what to revert? It's probably past your working hours by now, so likely I will just have a go at this myself in a few hours.
this is most likely part of the last change to leantar in order to make it use a temporary file to avoid tearing issues
IIRC there was a setting to make it put the temporary in the current folder instead of in /tmp or wherever
Should it be calling mktemp, which presumably landrun supports?
it's an off the shelf temp library
Could you link the relevant line?
in leangz it's pretty simple, tempfile::NamedTempFile and then persist to the target when we're done
Perhaps landrun should set TMPDIR to some directory that is writeable?

Kim Morrison said:

Mac Malone, if you have time to look at this before the next nightly release, could you ideally do the reverts yourself, or otherwise tell me what to revert?

Unfortunately, there have a number of changes built on top of the leantar support, so I would like to avoid reversion if possible.

Eric Wieser said:

Perhaps landrun should set TMPDIR to some directory that is writeable?

yes, my reading of the docs is that this should work
@Mario Carneiro, I feel like the hard link issue is more pressing then the temp dir one, as the linking is the current blocker.
what hardlink?
The cross-device link error in Kim's message.
oh that's the same problem
I recall the docs warning that it won't work if /tmp is a different filesystem than the target directory
which can be a problem since it is often tempfs instead of the normal (ext4 or something)
so setting TMPDIR=. should fix both issues
Probably worth making a new subdirectory and pointing TMPDIR at that instead?
While the TMPDIR workaround may be sufficient for Mathlib, a solution that does not have such a filesystem limitation altogther seems peferrable.
I guess Lake could set this, but it feels like this is a leantar internal issue.
there is a new_in method which could be set to the directory of the target file

@Kim Morrison I am confused as to why the bundled leantar is being used at all in Mathlib at the moment. I feel the simplest solution is just to avoid using the bundled leantar until we work out this issue.
released v0.1.19 but it needs to be tested in these environments

Mac Malone said:

Kim Morrison I am confused as to why the bundled leantar is being used at all in Mathlib at the moment. I feel the simplest solution is just to avoid using the bundled leantar until we work out this issue.

nightly-testing was failing because of incompatible traces between the Lean nightlies and the leantar cache on nightly-testing was using.

I'm not immediately finding the CI workflow runs exhibiting this, but we can try harder if that above sentence doesn't sound right to you! (Please let me know if I need to go searching for the relevant workflow run; I'm assuming for now I don't.)

Kim Morrison said:

nightly-testing was failing because of incompatible traces between the Lean nightlies and the leantar cache on nightly-testing was using.

Sorry, but I am not sure what this means. As far as I know, leantar's handling of traces did not change between 0.1.17 and 0.1.18. @Mario Carneiro?
that's correct
the only thing new in 0.1.18 is that all file writes go via temps now
and in 0.1.19 those temps are in the directory of the target file
actually, now that I think about it since leantar will be bundled I guess I should officially release v1.0. It's been stable for a while anyway
I'll do that for the first version of leantar that is bundled with a lean stable
@Mario Carneiro I think Kim is currently attempting to prepare a Lean release that includes the bundled leantar.
yeah, and I'll wait until we go through 3 versions of leantar in the next days when Kim finds bugs
whichever version survives is the one I will relabel to v1.0
I'm not yet clear on whether the bad .trace file error from yesterday is still a problem on the latest version

To clarify, the fix from v0.1.17 fixed deserialization for trace files which did not impact serialization, so the new leantar should be able to read trace files produced by old leantar (that old leantar could not roundtrip)
if you are still getting this error on >=0.1.17 then there is something else wrong
@Mario Carneiro I take it that 0.1.19 might address whatever went wrong here? https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/actions/runs/23073429676/job/67028833494

Mac Malone said:

Kim Morrison said:

nightly-testing was failing because of incompatible traces between the Lean nightlies and the leantar cache on nightly-testing was using.

Sorry, but I am not sure what this means. As far as I know, leantar's handling of traces did not change between 0.1.17 and 0.1.18. Mario Carneiro?

If you are still interested in examples of this or further clarification of why it failed I can provide them tomorrow, but the problematic version was .16 and the changes in .17 fixed it. The mathlib cache tool was using .16 until Friday when this started failing due to a change that started exercising the problematic roundtrip
Ah, okay, that makes sense.
(I actually did check if Mathlib was using 0.1.17 and it was now, because I thought I had remembered it using 0.1.16 still. It appears I was half right. :rofl: )
Could someone summarize for me here? Is the problem resolved? If so, how?

.17 fixes an issue in .16 (bad trace)
.18 introduces a new feature
.19 fixes an issue in .18
(technically .18 was also fixing an issue: it would not overwrite read-only files)
and @Kim Morrison the problem is probably resolved but I need someone (probably you) to test it in a relevant environment
.17 has been running in the CI without issues for the last couple of days

Marcelo Lynch said:

.17 has been running in the CI without issues for the last couple of days

You mean master CI, yes? It's nightly-testing and bump branch CI which is failing.

I would really prefer to not have to touch this further if possible.

@Mac Malone, can I leave to you to do whichever subset of these you think is sensible:

  • Working out if v0.1.19 will fix the nightly failures?
  • Deploying v0.1.19 in tonight's nightly?
  • Seeing if reverting the changes in Cache/ on nightly-testing (which switch to using the leantar bundled with lean), so it matches master, resolves the failures?

(I made those changes in Cache/ because of the leantar crash with a bad .trace file error reported at #nightly-testing > Mathlib status updates @ 💬 , visible in the nightly-testing logs first here: https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4-nightly-testing/actions/runs/23098470307/job/67094903229#step:33:3118)
how do I check the leantar version used in that run? Cache/IO.lean says .17 but if it's using a built in leantar then it may be different
That linked run was immediately before I switched nightly-testing's Cache to using the lean4 bundled leantar.
In particular, it is on commit https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4-nightly-testing/commit/733720bbcafe4bcedc44cdf5747b69fc87665f53
aha, it says installing leantar 0.1.16 in step cache (1/3)
so I think it's safe to say that .19 addresses all known issues in flight
and the rest is a matter of making sure the versions used are up to date, which I guess is @Mac Malone 's job

Okay

chore: update leantar to v0.1.19 lean#12938

is hopefully the solution then.

Kim Morrison said:

Mac Malone, can I leave to you to do whichever subset of these you think is sensible:

  • Working out if v0.1.19 will fix the nightly failures?
  • Deploying v0.1.19 in tonight's nightly?
  • Seeing if reverting the changes in Cache/ on nightly-testing (which switch to using the leantar bundled with lean), so it matches master, resolves the failures?

If the nightly with v0.1.19 does not work, I can take a look tomorrow. Unfortunately, I do not have anymore time today.
